propositions: The Gerrit Verify matrix currently enables pytest-cov coverage collection on all three Ubuntu Python cells (3.11, 3.12, 3.13) despite identical source and no version-specific branches, duplicating the same instrumentation work three times without distinct coverage verdicts.

Profiling shows coverage tracing adds 34 seconds of wall-clock time per uninstrumented cell (median A=511.16s with coverage, median B=477.16s without), confirming measurable runner occupancy cost from duplicate measurement.

Ubuntu Python 3.13 must become the sole coverage-instrumented cell while retaining all four matrix cells and both pytest tiers on all cells, with 3.11, 3.12, and macOS remaining uninstrumented behavioral-compatibility gates.

The workflow contract in test_ci_workflow_parity.py must enforce that exactly Ubuntu 3.13 receives both --cov and branch=true flags, all other cells receive neither, and the condition must use non-empty truthy and-slot with empty-string fallback to avoid GitHub Actions falsy trap.

OSS survey (Django, NumPy, SciPy) confirmed consensus: all three active projects selectively collect coverage on a primary or dedicated configuration while broader compatibility jobs run uninstrumented, with no documented rejection of this practice.

The change reduces aggregate traced work from three cells to one while preserving all assertions, test selections, OS variants, Python versions, and the unchanged branch=true and fail_under=70 gate, with back-out as a simple Gerrit revert.
